entities.summary: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano is a Mexican politician and civil engineer. A prominent social-democrat and the son of 51st president of Mexico Lázaro Cárdenas, he is a former Head of Government of Mexico City and a founder of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD). He ran for the presidency of Mexico three times, and his loss in the 1988 Mexican general election to Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) candidate Carlos Salinas de Gortari had long been considered the result of electoral fraud perpetrated by the ruling PRI, later acknowledged by Miguel de la Madrid, the incumbent president at the time of the election.

Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano: A Mexican Social-Democrat and Civil Engineer

Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, the son of Mexico's 51st president Lázaro Cárdenas, is a prominent figure in Mexican politics and civil engineering. He served as Head of Government of Mexico City and founded the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), a leading social-democratic party in Mexico. Cárdenas' three presidential bids, including his loss to Carlos Salinas de Gortari in 1988, have shaped Mexico's political landscape.

A key figure in Mexico's modern social-democratic movement, Cárdenas' influence can be seen in the country's electoral laws and public infrastructure projects. His legacy continues to be felt in Mexico City's governance and the PRD's ongoing efforts to promote social and economic reform.

This enduring presence in Mexican politics is a testament to Cárdenas' commitment to progressive values and his vision for a more equitable society.
